ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=x+b$ intersects the x-axis at point $C(4,0)$ and the y-axis at point $B$, and intersects with the hyperbola $y=\frac{m}{x}$ (where $x<0$) at point $A(-1,n)$. The line segment $OA$ is drawn. Find the analytic expression of the line and the hyperbola?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By substituting point $C$ into $y=x+b$, we get $b=-4$,\\
therefore $y=x-4$;\\
substituting point $A$ into $y=x-4$, we find $n=-5$,\\
therefore $A(-1, -5)$,\\
thus $m=-1\times (-5)=5$,\\
therefore $y=\frac{5}{x}$\\
therefore, the equations of the line and the hyperbola are \boxed{y=x-4} and \boxed{y=\frac{5}{x}}, respectively.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a rectangular coordinate system, with the origin labeled O; a straight line with positive slope goes from the lower left to the upper right, intersects the positive half-axis of the x-axis at C, and intersects near the negative half-axis of the y-axis at B; there is a branch of a hyperbola in the lower left, and it intersects the straight line near the third quadrant at A; the line segment OA has been drawn. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, point C(4,0) is on the straight line y=x+b. Substituting gives 0=4+b, so b=-4; therefore the straight line is y=x-4. Point A(-1,n) is also on this straight line. Substituting x=-1 gives n=-1-4=-5, so A=(-1,-5). Also because A is on the hyperbola y=m/x, substituting gives -5=m/(-1), which is equivalent to m=(-1)(-5)=5, so the hyperbola is y=5/x.
